whatThisIs: What HAI-1 claims it can do, published by HAI so that tools can read it without HAI installed. Every row is the author of HAI describing HAI, not an independent assessment. The evidence field is the part to read: "hub" means someone watched it work on a hub on that date, "simulated" means nobody has. Nothing here says anything about your hub, and nothing here is a comment on any other app or engine: it describes HAI and only HAI.

statusMeanings.Runs: Built, checked, read back and simulated, and not refused by the runtime. The evidence field says whether anyone has seen it run on a hub.
statusMeanings.Format: Can be written, will not act. A rule can use it and HAI checks and simulates it, but the runtime deliberately refuses to carry it out yet; the note says why.
statusMeanings.Partial: Some of it works. The note says what is missing.
statusMeanings.Missing: Not built. HAI has no equivalent; the note says why.

evidenceMeanings.hub: Seen working on a hub on the date given.
evidenceMeanings.simulated: Built and simulated, but nobody has watched it run. It may still be wrong on a hub.
